records.name: Design Advocacy Group (DAG)
records.summary: A public forum that pushes for better design and fairer outcomes in Philadelphia's planning, architecture, preservation and building projects. It holds monthly public events and publishes advocacy articles.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly public event, read the advocacy articles, or join the email list as a free member.

schedule.text: Monthly events, each posted with its own date and time. No regular day or time is set.

locations.label: Village of Industry and Art (event venue)

cost.text: Membership is free. The site does not list a price for the monthly events.

first_step.how: Come to the talk on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 320 S Broad St, 5:30 to 7 pm. Registration is not required, but an RSVP helps the organizers plan.
first_step.basis: Events are public, registration is not required, and membership is a simple free email sign-up with no application or approval step.
first_step.what_to_expect: The October talk runs 5:30 to 7 pm and includes light refreshments. Speakers from regional planning, transit and city planning agencies will talk about neighborhoods built around transit stops.
first_visit_tips: The event page gives the venue but no parking or transit details, so check the route before you go.
If you want updates without attending, the Become a Member page has a free email sign-up.

records.notes: The October talk page header misspells the venue name; the body spells it correctly. Events are not always at the same venue, and the November 19, 2026 event is listed on the homepage without details. The RSVP for the October talk goes to an outside event page that was not visited. The Forum page is for opinion articles by individual authors, not meetings. No accessibility, parking or transit notes were found on the site.

records.name: Dignity Philadelphia
records.summary: A Catholic community for LGBTQ+ Catholics in Philadelphia. Members gather for Sunday Mass in Center City, join online Masses and discussion nights, and get email updates about events.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in person or online, join a Zoom discussion, or read the group's quarterly magazine. Members also get email updates about services and events, and can take part in the group's projects, such as its oral history project.

schedule.text: Sunday Mass in person at 7 pm. Some Masses and discussion nights are held on Zoom instead. The Mass Schedule and Events page lists the dates.

locations.label: The Church of St. Luke and the Epiphany (Sunday Mass)
locations.transit: A few blocks from the Broad Street Line, the Market-Frankford Line, Regional Rail and several SEPTA bus routes, per the group's site

cost.text: No amounts are published. Membership dues pay for weekly costs, and scholarships are available; contact the group for details.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday Mass at 7 pm at 330 S 13th Street. The site also lists online Masses on Zoom on some dates.
first_step.basis: Mass times, the street address and parking notes are posted publicly, and a contact email is listed. The site does not describe a first visit or say whether visitors need to sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday Mass is at 7 pm in the church at 330 S 13th Street, and some services and discussion nights are on Zoom. The site does not describe what a service is like or what to wear. Arriving a few minutes early gives you time to find a seat.
first_visit_tips: Center City street parking is free on Sundays. The church's own lot is no longer available; the site lists a discounted rate at the EZ Lot, 515 S 15th St, and says to contact the group for the code.
Several transit lines are a few blocks away, including the Broad Street Line, the Market-Frankford Line and Regional Rail.

records.notes: The site does not say whether people who are not members may attend Mass, so drop_in rests on the public Mass listing alone. The membership page says membership is for LGBTQ+ Catholics and does not say whether allies may join. Mail-in membership forms exist; the record does not include the mailing details. The Mass Schedule page also lists a fall 2026 liturgy discussion and an oral history project; dated items are kept out of schedule text.

records.name: Discovery Pathways
records.summary: A South Philadelphia nonprofit that teaches outdoor and environmental skills to young people and adults. Its programs include boating, fishing, youth leadership, dragon boating and greening work in parks and along waterways.
records.what_you_do: Join a free boating or fishing day at FDR Park, take part in youth leadership or community greening work, paddle with the dragon boat team, or sign up to volunteer through the volunteer form.

schedule.text: Free family fishing on Wednesdays, 4 to 6:30 pm, and free boating days on select Saturdays, 10 am to 1:30 pm, at FDR Park. The events calendar lists the specific dates.

locations.label: Boathouse at FDR Park (boating and fishing days)

cost.text: Boating days and family fishing at FDR Park are free, and field trips are free for grades K to 12 public school classes. The site did not state prices for its other programs.

first_step.how: Come to a free boating day at FDR Park on a Saturday from 10 am to 1:30 pm. Boating needs no registration and no experience.
first_step.basis: The FDR boating and fishing programs are free and open to all ages, boating needs no experience, and the site says no pre-registration is needed for boating.
first_step.what_to_expect: Boating days provide rowboats, kayaks and canoes with instruction, and children must come with a guardian. Family fishing on Wednesdays from 4 to 6:30 pm teaches people how to fish, with rods and bait provided.
first_visit_tips: The site does not say whether life jackets are provided, so ask the group before you go.
The site gives no parking or transit details for FDR Park, so check the route in advance.

records.notes: The FDR program page lists one June boating date that falls on a Thursday; the events calendar uses Saturdays, so the Saturday pattern was used. The volunteer form's youngest age option is 18, though no minimum age is written. No background check or clearance is mentioned for volunteers. Life jacket provision and fishing registration are not stated. The events calendar offers an iCal subscription (webcal link) and a direct .ics download; the direct download is recorded as the calendar feed.

records.name: Djola History and Genealogy Society
records.summary: A history and genealogy society for people whose African ancestry DNA results link them to the Djola family. It shares Djola history, oral histories, and research on DNA, places, and language.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member to get help researching your family history and to take part in workshops, tours and events. You can also sign up for the newsletter to hear about news and events.

schedule.text: The site lists general hours: Monday to Friday, 6:30 to 9 pm, and Saturday and Sunday, 8 am to 6 pm, Eastern time. It does not say what these hours are for. The membership page says the society hosts Zoom meetings every other week, with no days or times given.

cost.text: Membership is $25 a year or $250 for life, paid by Zelle or Cash App as the site lists. Donations are also accepted.

first_step.how: Send the society a message through the Become a Member page with your full name, email and phone number, and ask how to join.
first_step.basis: Joining means paying dues and then being given a password after you message the society, and the site does not say whether non-members can visit or attend events.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a visit. Members are promised help with family research, hard to find information on Djola history, and invitations to workshops, tours and events.
first_visit_tips: The site gives no street address, only a city and ZIP code, so ask where any gathering takes place before you go.

records.notes: Status is dormant under the dated-evidence rule. The newest dated item on the news page is from August 2021, and the other dated items are from 2019 and January 2021. The hours, Zoom statement and membership text are undated, so they do not set the status. Verdict kept as publish; the owner may want to review whether a dormant group stays visible. Dues are paid through personal payment apps; the record reports only the methods named and no account details. The site frames the society around Djola people and descendants but does not say membership is limited to them. The membership form asks for contact details in a message, and the page says a password is sent after joining.

records.name: Donte Wylie Foundation
records.summary: A group in Philadelphia that works on gun violence, with a space for people affected by violence, including people who have hurt others, to heal and work toward fewer shootings.
records.what_you_do: Contact the foundation by phone or email to ask about volunteering or partnering. The site names one program, Yesterday's YOUth Commission for Change, and lists no regular meetings or upcoming events.

schedule.text: No regular meetings or events are listed on the site. Ask the foundation how to take part.

first_step.how: Email info@thedontewyliefoundation.com or call 267-281-3762 and ask how to volunteer or take part in the foundation's work.
first_step.basis: The site names no regular meetings, sessions or events, so the way in is unclear until you ask.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a visit, a meeting or a regular session. Its one stated next step is to get in touch with questions about volunteering or partnering.
first_visit_tips: The only address on the site is a P.O. Box, so ask where any gathering takes place before you go.

records.notes: The home page states the foundation serves survivors of violence, people who have caused harm, and community members, which supports the summary. The about page returned a 404. The site has no dated items: the 2019 copyright line is not evidence, and the events section says there are no events at the moment, so the status is probably_active on a working site with no dates. One web search found no 2025 or 2026 events or volunteer listings for the foundation; an unrelated 2026 volunteer posting that names another organization was not used, and search results about a family member were not used. The only address is a P.O. Box, not a meeting place. Donations go through an outside payment link, which is not recorded.

records.name: East Falls Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church in East Falls with Sunday worship, children's care, and small Bible study groups that meet in person or online.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship (nursery and Sunday school for children), join a Monday evening or Thursday small group, or come to the All Saints candle lighting.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am, with Sunday School for children from September to June. Small Bible study groups meet in series: Monday evenings at 7:30 pm in person, and Thursday evenings at 7 pm in person or 7:30 pm online.

cost.text: The site does not list costs for worship, Sunday School or the small groups.

access.notes: A ramp leads into the building and the sanctuary. The hall, which has the bathroom and nursery, is up three steps with a chair lift, and a chair lift also serves the basement fellowship hall.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am at 3800 Vaux Street. For the Thursday small groups, sign up through the linked form on the site.
first_step.basis: The worship page says visitors are glad to be there, and the All Saints event says non-religious visitors are welcome; the Thursday groups have a clear sign-up form.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 10:30 am in the sanctuary, with traditional hymns, choral music, printed liturgy and prayer. Dress ranges from Sunday best to jeans, and children may stay in the sanctuary or go to Sunday School after the children's sermon. Communion is served on the first Sunday of each month, and servers bring it to people who cannot come forward. The nursery is staffed by two background-checked adult caregivers.
first_visit_tips: Online worship is also available; the site has a sign-up link at the top of the page.
The site gives no parking or transit details, so check the route before you go.

records.notes: Sunday School age ranges: the children's page says the younger class is roughly ages 4 to second grade and the older class roughly 3rd to 6th grade; the worship page says roughly ages 4 to 12. The homepage gives the nursery as through about age 3. The All Saints candle lighting is a one time November 2 event and is not in the record. The background check applies to nursery staff only, not to families or visitors. The who-we-are page says members come from many church backgrounds and welcomes women and LGBTQ+ people to church leadership; that is not in the record. The rating 4 rests on the worship welcome lines and the open Sunday time; the site has no dedicated new here page.

records.name: East Passyunk Opera Project (ePOP)
records.summary: A Philadelphia opera company that brings opera, musical theater and art song into neighborhood venues, with free or low-cost shows and free community concerts.
records.what_you_do: Attend a show or free community concert, bring a child to a family opera session, join the mailing list, or support the work through its fiscal sponsor, Fractured Atlas.

schedule.text: No weekly schedule. Shows, masterclasses and community concerts are posted on the events page as they are booked.

locations.label: Office address (shows are held at other venues)

cost.text: The company describes its shows as free or low cost, and its community concerts as free. The events list does not show ticket prices, so check each event's Learn more page.

first_step.how: Pick a show or free concert from the events page and open its Learn more link for the details.
first_step.basis: Shows are public and each event has a Learn more link, but the site does not show ticket prices, RSVP steps or how far ahead shows are announced.
first_step.what_to_expect: ePOP performs opera, musical theater and art song in neighborhood venues. A family session, The Wondrous World of Opera, is listed for children from preschool to third grade and their families. The site does not say how long a show runs or what to wear.
first_visit_tips: Open the Learn more link for each event to find its ticket price before you go.
Venues change by event; the events list names places such as Dilworth Park and the Academy of Vocal Arts' Helen Corning Warden Theater for some shows.

records.notes: The events page lists 3 upcoming events, including a November 21, 2026 masterclass, and 27 past events back to December 2022; the most recent past event with a full date is June 18, 2026, which sets the last sign of life. A few September and early October 2026 dates are still listed as upcoming. Ticket prices, RSVP steps and venues for most events are not on the events page. The news page has headlines but no publication dates; it covers the Philly Pride Arts Festival, whose 2026 edition is not recorded as a separate group. The office address is not a show venue. The 2020 copyright line is not used as evidence. The social links are the group's own contact links; no facts were taken from them.
